- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by immediate drop, reduce peak value by 5–10% to account for volatility overreaction.  
- If forecast mean is significantly below recent 5-day average, increase by 2–3% to reflect mean reversion toward recent trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.1–0.6), apply slight lag correction: forecast = previous 7-day average + 0.5×(true - previous 7-day avg) to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast consistently underestimates true values in 30-day window, apply 1–2% upward bias for next forecast, especially if sentiment is rising.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true values, apply 1–2% downward bias, especially if sentiment is falling or mixed.
